class.peasant.family.CHN: into a family of tenant farmers
class.landowner.family.CHN: into a gentry family of scholar-landowners
class.noble.family.CHN: into the family of a high official
prof.farmer.desc.CHN: Rice or millet on someone else’s land. Half the harvest goes to the landlord.
prof.laborer.desc.CHN: A carrying pole on your shoulders, sacks on the wharf, any job for a day’s pay.
prof.artisan.desc.CHN: Lacquer, bronze, paper, woodcarving — every trade has its own street and its own guild.
prof.weaver.desc.CHN: Silkworms, skeins and the loom. Silk goes to the tax collector, the market and overseas.
prof.midwife.desc.CHN: You deliver babies and know the herbs and rites. No household manages without you.
prof.merchant.desc.CHN: Confucians call trade a lowly calling — but merchants have money, and money opens many doors.
prof.sailor.desc.CHN: Barges on the Grand Canal, junks along the coast. The pay is decent, but water forgives no mistakes.
prof.soldier.desc.CHN: “Good iron isn’t made into nails” — soldiers get little respect, but they are fed. Frontier, garrisons and campaigns.
prof.scribe.desc.CHN: You copy tax registers and petitions at the county office. The salary is small, but everyone knows a lot depends on you.
prof.physician.desc.CHN: Pulse reading, herbs, needles and moxa. You learn from ancient treatises and printed books of prescriptions.
prof.priest.desc.CHN: Rites, exorcisms, talismans and memorial services. People send for you when trouble strikes.
prof.landholder.desc.CHN: You rent your paddies to tenants, read the classics and make sure the sons prepare for the examinations.
prof.magistrate.desc.CHN: You are the “father and mother of the people” of a whole prefecture: courts, taxes, dikes and famine. Every three years, a new posting.
prof.matron.as.CHN: the mistress of a great house
prof.matron.desc.CHN: Servants, storerooms, a mother-in-law, concubines, daughters’ dowries — it’s all on you.
prof.household_slave.desc.CHN: You are registered to your master’s house and not free to leave. Kitchen, errands, sedan chair.
prof.field_slave.desc.CHN: You work the master’s fields for food. You cannot leave and there is no one to complain to.
prof.officer.desc.CHN: You command a hundred soldiers. More pay — and the blame for any defeat.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.CHN: Your own workshop, apprentices and a seat in the guild.
prof.shipowner.desc.CHN: Your boats ply the canals and the southern seas. Huge profits, and as many worries.
prof.official.desc.CHN: A winged cap, a seal and a salary from the treasury. People bow to you — and the censors watch you.
prof.overseer.desc.CHN: The master has trusted you with the estate and the other servants. Still a bondservant — but with the keys.
prof.exam_scholar.desc: Years over the classics for the examinations. Pass, and you become an official; fail, and you teach other people’s children.
prof.monk.desc: A shaven head, sutras, alms and the quiet of the monastery. The family loses a worker but gains merit.
prof.tea_grower.desc: Tea bushes on mountain terraces, the spring picking before dawn and a state monopoly on sales.
prof.porcelain_maker.desc: Clay, the wheel and a dragon kiln climbing the hillside. One good firing feeds you for a year.
prof.salt_merchant.desc: Salt is a state monopoly. Buy salt certificates from the treasury and you grow rich — unless the bribes ruin you first.
prof.storyteller.desc: You tell tales of the Three Kingdoms and noble outlaws in pleasure grounds and teahouses. Paid in coppers and laughter.
lifestyle.food.plain.desc.CHN: Rice or millet, vegetables, bean curd
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.CHN: Fish, pork, fruit, good tea. Good for your health
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.CHN: Dozens of dishes, rice wine, guests and poems. Expensive
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.CHN: Archery, riding and Daoist daoyin exercises
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.CHN: Incense, talismans, prayers to Guanyin and the Medicine Buddha
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.CHN: A physician reads your pulse and prescribes decoctions. Expensive, but safer
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.CHN: A basin of water, and the river in summer
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.CHN: Town bathhouses with hot water and gossip. Must live in a city
focus.learn.desc.CHN: A teacher, the Thousand Character Classic and brush copybooks. The family pays
focus.study.desc.CHN: The Confucian canon, essays, preparing for the examinations. Costs money
focus.religion.desc.CHN: Ancestral tablets, incense, temples and monasteries
focus.rest.desc.CHN: Teahouses, shows, friends and rice wine
vice.gambler.CHN: gambles — at dice and cricket fights
ev.a_good_harvest.text.2.CHN: A generous year: the rice heads bow to the water and the granary is full to the rafters. Even the landlord smiled as he took his share.
ev.c_child_fall.text.CHN: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} climbed the old mulberry tree by the road and fell. The arm is swollen and hangs wrong. {g=npc_sex:He|She} is trying very hard not to cry.
ev.a_inheritance.text.CHN: The inheritance isn’t divided yet, and {npc} already claims the best rice fields: “I looked after the old man while you were off who knows where.” And {g=npc_sex:he|she} is not entirely wrong.
ev.c_trade_high.estates.ok.CHN: {npc} rides round the estates, measuring fields and arguing with tenants. The stewards already miss the old days.
ev.c_teacher.home_teach.ok.CHN: In the evenings the two of you sit over the copybook. You’ve discovered you’d long forgotten half the characters yourself.
